name: B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase

function.text: BRAF encodes a RAF-family serine/threonine kinase that relays signals through the MAPK/ERK pathway to regulate cell growth and differentiation.

germline.text: Retained constitutional disease associations include Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome (autosomal dominant). Pathogenicity and inheritance depend on the specific allele and disorder.

somatic.text: Somatic activating BRAF mutations occur in melanoma, colorectal and thyroid carcinomas, lung carcinoma, and hairy cell leukemia, among other neoplasms. Interpretation depends on the specific alteration and tumor context; a generic BRAF finding does not establish a V600E mechanism.

function.text: BRAF encodes a serine/threonine kinase in the RAF family that relays growth signals through the MAPK/ERK pathway. This signaling pathway helps regulate cell division, differentiation, and secretion. Activating changes in BRAF can increase this signaling output; V600E is a well-characterized example, but the gene's normal role is to transmit regulated signals rather than maintain continuous pathway activation.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include Cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic activating BRAF mutations occur in melanoma, colorectal and thyroid carcinomas, lung carcinoma, and hairy cell leukemia, among other neoplasms.
